2026-11-10.title: Second Tuesday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-10.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
2026-11-10.verse: Then from the cloud came a voice that said, “This is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him!”
theo: Peter, near the end of his life, remembers the mountain: “we had been eyewitnesses of his majesty… We ourselves heard this voice come from heaven.” The faith of the Church rests on eyewitnesses and on the prophetic word, “a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns.”

On the mountain Jesus prays and is transfigured; Moses and Elijah speak with him of his departure in Jerusalem. The glory prepares the disciples for the Cross. The Church, in her last season, looks toward the same glory: the day when the Morning Star rises in our hearts.
outline: Ask: when have you glimpsed God's glory?
Our faith rests on apostolic witness, not clever myths.
The Father points to the Son.
The Transfiguration strengthens us for suffering.
“This is my Son: listen to him.”
live: Read today's Gospel slowly and keep one phrase.
Give ten minutes to silent prayer today.
2026-11-10.prayer: Lord Jesus, transfigured in glory, let me listen to you and be changed by your light, until the day dawns and the Morning Star rises in my heart. Amen.

2026-11-10.question: What does Jesus want me to hear today?

homily: Dear friends, near the end of his life Peter remembers the mountain: we had been eyewitnesses of his majesty; we ourselves heard this voice come from heaven while we were with him on the holy mountain (2 Peter 1:16–18). The faith of the Church rests on eyewitnesses and on the prophetic word.

That word is like a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts (2 Peter 1:19). On the mountain of the Transfiguration Jesus' face shone, and a voice came from the cloud: this is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him (Luke 9:35).

In the dark places of life we have God's word as our lamp. The Father's command, listen to him, is for us too. This week let us read the Gospel for ten minutes each day and quietly contemplate the face of Jesus. Amen.
kids: Children, on the mountain Jesus' face shone like the sun. God said: listen to him. Read one word of Jesus in the Bible today!

intro: Peter's eyewitness memory of the Transfiguration.

sub: Moses' face shone after speaking with God.
Jesus' face changes as he prays.
q: Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone because he had been talking with God.
And while he was praying, the appearance of his face changed, and his clothes became dazzling white.
points.apply: Give ten minutes to silent prayer.

sub: The psalmist longs to see God's face.
In Jesus the face of God shines on us.
q: “Come,” my heart says, “seek his face!” Your face, LORD, do I seek.
Then from the cloud came a voice that said, “This is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him!”
points.apply: Read the Gospel slowly and keep one phrase.

sub: The prophetic word is a lamp until the day dawns.
The Church waits for the Morning Star.
q: The LORD make his face to shine upon you, and be gracious to you.
Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.”
points.apply: Bless your family with Numbers 6:24–26 tonight.

concl: The glory of the mountain is the promise of our future.
Let us listen to the Son.
